details.purpose: *To record the results of visual acuity assessments, which are typically performed by quantifying the individual's ability to detect, resolve or identify visual differences or symbols. (en)
details.use:
*Use to record a single assessment of visual acuity per event.
Use both for assessments attempting to identify the highest attainable visual acuity, as well as those where the visual acuity under special conditions is of interest.
Use the 'Result'-cluster to record the primary notation of the assessment, typically only using one of the contained elements per event.
Use the 'Derived Results' Cluster to record any number of conversions or derivations into other notations.
Use the 'Supplementary results'-SLOT for structured results not covered by other elements.
Use the 'Visual aid per eye' SLOT to record what was positioned in front of the eye(s) during the assessment. This allows flexible combination of aids to be recorded, including multiple corrections in front of the same eye.
Population of 'Visual aid type' element is recommended under all circumstances. Use the value "unaided" for uncorrected tests where nothing was positioned in front of the tested eye(s).
Use this archetype for tests of minimum detectable, resolveable or recognizable visual acuity as well as reading acuity, but consider specifying this using the 'Perceptive Task' element. (en)
details.misuse:
*Not to be used to record multiple visual acuity tests in one event.
The "Result" cluster is not to be used to record the same visual acuity test in multiple converted units - only the primary notation is to be documented there. If the same test result is to be converted to other units, use the "derived result" cluster for all conversion results.
Not to be used for assessments of fixation behaviour or observations of eye movements (e.g. fixes and follows, central steady maintained fixation). No appropriate archetype is available for this at the time of writing.
Not to be used for assessing light projection, use 'OBSERVATION.light_projection_test' instead. (en)

items.items: A test to quantify an individual's visual acuity as a measure of the ability to detect, resolve or recognize visual details.
The eye which was examined, or both eyes in case of a binocular test.
'Both eyes' may only be used for test of binocular visual acuity.
The aid was positioned in front of the left eye.
The aid was positioned in front of the left eye.
The type of symbol used to assess visual acuity.
Coding with a terminology is recommended. Free text entry should only be permitted if no appropriate coded value is available.
The type of chart or card used to measure visual acuity.
Coding with a terminology is recommended. Free text entry should only be permitted if no appropriate coded value is available.
Details of the devices used provide a stimulus to be resolved by the eye being tested, such as a chart, projector or digital display.
Additional narrative about the measurement, not captured in other fields.
A categorisation of the testing distance.
Boundary definitions may vary, therefore population of the 'Testing distance' element is encouraged, especially for intermediate or near distances.
Description of any incidental factors related to the state of the subject which may affect clinical interpretation of the measurement.
Examples: 'Patient was confused', "Lid held open by hand" "Eccentric Fixation".
Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.
Details to explicitly record that this test was not performed.
Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.
For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.
The highest level of visual function demonstrated by the individual during qualitative assessment.
Not to be used for light projection testing. Use OBSERVATION.light_projection_test archetype for this purpose. Higher ordinal values represent better visual function.
A grouping of calculated or estimated visual acuity result values derived by conversion from the primary recorded result.
The test was performed at near distance.
The test was performed at intermediate distance.
The test was performed at far distance.
Information on the way the visual stimulus is displayed.
Allows for the capture of basic information where additional detail about the type or device name of the stimulus are unknown.
Keeler acuity cards were used, a type of grating-based preferential looking test.
Background luminance of the visual stimulus, such as the white background on a chart.
Candela per square meter is equivalent to the non-SI unit 'nit'.
The difference between stimulus and background luminance divided by background luminance.
The difference between maximum and minimum luminance of the stimulus divided by their sum.
The ambient illuminance in the room where the visual acuity testing is taking place.
A cluster describing what type of visual aid was used during the test, and which eye it was positioned in front of.
Where multiple devices are positioned in front of the same eye, this cluster is expected to be used once for each.
The visual acuity measured and expressed as a decimal notation.
The visual acuity measured and expressed as a metre Snellen ratio or M-Scale ratio.

For Snellen ratio notation, the numerator is typically a reference distance of six meters, regardless of the real testing distance. For M-Scale notation, the numerator should be equal to to the real testing distance. To avoid ambiguity, populate the 'Testing distance' element, especially if the M-Scale notation is used.
The visual acuity measured and expressed as a feet Snellen ratio.
A reference distance of 20 feet is often used as the default numerator. Usethe 'Testing distance' element to avoid ambiguity.
The visual acuity measured and expressed as the base-10 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (MAR).
Sometimes referred to as 'logRAD' in reading acuity tests.
N point font size notation result
The N point font size of the smallest recognized line or text.
Strictly not a unit of visual acuity but a measure of stimulus size.
The Jaeger font size of the smallest recognized line of text.
Strictly not a unit of visual acuity but a measure of stimulus size.
Visual acuity in decimal notation, derived from the primary recording.
Visual acuity in metre ratio (Snellen or M-Score) notation, derived from the primary recording.
Visual acuity in feet (Snellen) ratio notation, derived from the primary recording.
Visual acuity in logMAR notation, derived from the primary recording.
Not to be used for information about how the test was performed or patient circumstances affecting result.
The visual acuity measured and expressed using the logarithmic 5-score notation, widely used in China.
Defined as 5 minus the LogMAR result, part of the Chinese national standard GB11533-1989.
The visual acuity measured and expressed as the ETDRS letter score.

Caution: The ETDRS score is inclusive of the 30 letters that may be presented at 1m distance, which are added to the results of testing at 4m distance. See ETDRS report number 7 in References. A letter score of 85 is equivalent to 20/20, 1.0 decimal, 0.0 logMAR.
Visual acuity as ETDRS notation, derived from the primary recording.

Caution: The ETDRS score is inclusive of the 30 letters that may be presented at 1m distance, which are added to the results of testing at 4m distance. See ETDRS report number 7 in References. A letter score of 85 is equivalent to 20/20, 1.0 decimal, 0.0 logMAR.
Classification of the test and its result as 'best corrected', 'best recorded' visual acuity, or similar statements.
These classifiers do not contain information on the actual correction used. It is encouraged to record the specific aids used within 'Visual aid per eye' clusters.
This result is classified as a Best Corrected Visual Acuity.
This result is classified as a Best Recorded Visual Acuity.
Information specifying the type of device, or lack of a device positioned in front of one of the eyes.

Avoid using the generic value "Corrected" where the device or provenance of corrective values are known.
Coding with a terminology is recommended. Free text entry should only be permitted if no appropriate coded value is available.
A correction with powers based on an autorefraction test.
A correction with powers based on a subjective refraction.
A contact lens with a rigid optical center, including hybrid lenses.
A soft contact lens with a soft optical center.
A correction with powers based on a retinoscopy test.
Lenses without a known provenance or source of the powers.
A lens used to intentionally blur the vision in that eye while the other eye is tested.
A device with one or multiple small holes acting as apertures.
A correction with values based on subjective overrefraction was used.
There is explicitly nothing in front of the eye during the visual acuity testing, also referred to as "uncorrected".
Details on the use of ancillary lighting sources, including brightness acuity testing and glare lights.
The eye in front of which the visual aid was positioned.

For monocular tests where the partner eye is fully occluded, the assumption is that the visual aid is positioned in front of the eye being tested. In these circumstances automated population from the 'Eye examined' element is possible.

Information on single optotypes where the main score was based on a whole line of optotypes. Negative: Number incorrect optotypes in the last line that was marked as correct. Positive: The number of correct optotypes in the first line that was marked as incorrect. "Partial" code indicates some unspecified number of optotypes were missed in the smallest scored line.
Some symbols were not read correctly in the smallest line that was scored as being successfully read.
The distance between the tested eye and the (apparent) location of the stimulus.
The stimulus may be a virtual image.
A note indicating that the addition or use of another type of aid did not result in a better test result.

Used where a determination of the exact visual acuity with the additional correction (in another event) was not performed, typically because it was deemed irrelevant for lack of improvement. Coding with a terminology is recommended. Free text entry should only be permitted if no appropriate coded value is available.
No improvement with an additional pinhole placed in front of the tested eye.
No improvement with corrective lenses based on subjective refraction.
Statement describing the condition of the individual's pupils during the test.

The physical examination of the eye will be recorded using the CLUSTER.exam-eye family of archetypes. Coding with a terminology is recommended. Free text entry should only be permitted if no appropriate coded value is available.
The pupil is in its natural physiological state without pharmacological intervention or pathological changes.
The pupil was dilated due to prior administration of mydriatic agents.
The pupil was constricted due to prior administration of miotic agents.
The pupil was in an unphysiological state due to disease, trauma, or structural abnormalities.
A grouping of data elements to represent the primary notation of the visual acuity assessment result.
Typically, only one result should be populated. Converted or derived values should be stored in the appropriate element in the 'Derived result' cluster.
The refractive power that is equal in all meridians.
Used as the base correction upon which cylinder and axis are applied.
Structured details about the device used as a visual aid during testing, such as a phoropter, trial frame, glasses, or contact lenses.
The refractive power added to the spherical correction at the meridian 90° from the cylinder axis to compensate for astigmatism.
The orientation of the cylinder in degrees.
By convention, the axis of the cylinder is defined by its meridian of zero power.
The additional spherical lens power for near vision.
Physical objects other than charts or cards.
Berkeley rudimentary vision test (BRVT) was used.
A near reading card with segments of text was used.
LEA gratings were used, a type of a grating-based preferential looking test.
Teller acuity cards were used, a type of grating-based preferential looking test.
The Cardiff acuity test was used, a type of vanishing optotype-based preferential looking test.
An Allen picture test was used.
A Cambridge crowding card test was used.
A Minnesota Low Vision Reading (MNREAD) reading acuity chart was used.
A Radner reading chart was used.
A Freiburg visual acuity test (FrACT) was used.
A Sheridan Gardiner test was used.
A chart presented as a virtual image inside a device, such as an autorefractor.
The number of cycles (line pairs) per centimetre of the finest grating pattern recognized by the individual.
Strictly not a unit of visual acuity but a measure of stimulus size.
The visual acuity measured and expressed as the number of pairs of black and white lines (cycles) that subtend an angle of one degree at the tested eye.
Used in grating based tests such as Teller acuity cards.
Visual acuity as cycles per degree, derived by conversion from the primary recording.
No improvement with corrective lenses based on an autorefraction test.
No improvement with a soft contact lens.
No improvement with corrective lenses based on retinoscopy.
No improvement with a hard contact lens.
A Sonksen Silver test was used.
Information on whether the correction used was based on a measurement of the refractive error in a cycloplegic state.
The correction used was based on a measurement of refractive error in a cycloplegic state.
The correction used was based on a measurement of refractive error in a non-cycloplegic state.
No improvement with an unspecified further correction.
Additional structured details on visual acuity test result not captured in other data elements.
Examples include specifying the card scored in a Cardiff acuity test, or supplementary results on reading visual acuity tests.
A statement on the contrast level of the test.
Note that the majority of visual acuity tests are performed under high contrast conditions. Where possible, population of quantitative elements on contrast is encouraged.
The test was performed with high contrast.
The test was performed with low contrast.
Details on how the optotypes were presented, including statements on crowding.
A lens used with the intention of adding refractive error.
A categorical statement on whether a crowding effect is expected to be induced by the visual stimulus.
Additional detail on the degree of crowding, and presence of crowding bars can be recorded using the 'Optotype presentation details' SLOT.
The stimulus was presented in a manner thought to induce a crowding effect.
The stimulus was presented in a manner thought to induce no crowding effect.
Type of light sources used in addition to the typical room, stimulus or chart lighting.
Coding with a terminology is recommended. Free text entry should only be permitted if no appropriate coded value is available.
A light source, or multiple light sources were directed at the eye to induce glare.
A handheld ganzfeld illumination device was used to simulate environmental brightness.
Narrative comment about the specific visual aid used.
The type of perceptual task endpoint that the result represents.
Reading visual acuity expressed LogMAR is sometimes referred to as LogRAD. Supplementary results of reading visual acuity tests can be recorded via the 'supplementary results' slot.
A measurement of the ability to distinguish two separate objects as distinct.
A measurement of the smallest visual angle at which text can be read.
The presumed adaptation state of the visual system during testing.
This is a categorical description of the individual's presumed retinal adaptation state, not a measurement of the ambient lighting.
The individual is adapted to high luminance conditions.
The individual is in a transitional adaptation state between photopic and scotopic.
The individual is adapted to low luminance conditions.
The individual was unable to identify the absence or presence of light.
The individual correctly identified the absence or presence of light.
An electronic or computerized ETRDS testing protocol was used.
The Amblyopia Treatment Study HOTV testing protocol was used.
A measurement of the ability to detect a visual object.
A measurement of the ability to recognize and identify a visual object.
The aid was positioned in front of the left eye.
The aid was positioned in front of the left eye.
